subtitle: Every Twins position player on the active roster at any point in September 2026: 22 hitters. 19 pitchers excluded. April through September are regular-season games in that month. Last 10 is each hitter’s last 10 games with a plate appearance on or before September 30. A month with no plate appearances is blank.
footnote1: Footnote 1. Archetype picks the contact-quality rate shown for that hitter. Damage rate is the share of tracked fair batted balls with exit velocity of at least 95 mph and launch angle of at least 10 degrees. Tracked fair batted balls are Statcast pitches with type X and non-null exit velocity and launch angle. Barrel rate is Statcast barrel% (launch_speed_angle = 6) on that same denominator. The groups use 2026 regular-season competitive contact, which is those batted balls excluding bunts. A hitter is Damage when average exit velocity is at least 1.0 mph above the pooled MLB average of 88.0 mph. That is the power and high-exit-velocity group, graded on damage rate. A hitter is Barrel when average exit velocity is below that line. That is the average-exit-velocity group, graded on barrel rate. The two groups do not have to be the same size. Hitters with fewer than 30 competitive batted balls stay unclassified and the contact cells are blank. The superscript 1 marks Brooks Lee, Luke Keaschall, and Byron Buxton. Brooks Lee is the damage example. Luke Keaschall is the barrel example. Byron Buxton is Damage because he is a power and high-exit-velocity hitter. 2026 MLB average EV on competitive contact was 88.0 mph (n=124,098). 2026 MLB barrel rate was 7.7% (n=124,098 tracked batted balls, bunts included in that denominator). Brooks Lee’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 87.8 mph (n=488) and his barrel rate was 4.5%. Avg EV 87.8 mph is near the league average 88.0. Damage because he is a power hitter, the damage example. Final label: Damage. Luke Keaschall’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 84.8 mph (n=450) and his barrel rate was 3.8%. Avg EV 84.8 mph is below the league average 88.0. Barrel because he is an average-EV hitter, the barrel example. Final label: Barrel. Byron Buxton’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 90.2 mph (n=272) and his barrel rate was 15.8%. Avg EV 90.2 mph is +2.2 versus the league average 88.0. Damage because he is a power / high-EV hitter. Final label: Damage.
footnote2: Execution uses three equally weighted inputs. Each rate is divided by the MLB pooled league rate for the same definition, the three ratios are averaged, and the result is multiplied by 100. Composite = 100 × ((RISP knock-in / league RISP knock-in) + (move-over / league move-over) + (QAB / league QAB)) / 3. A composite of 100 is league average. The raw rates are not averaged together, because they sit on different scales. RISP knock-in is the share of plate appearances that begin with a runner on second and/or third in which the batter is credited with at least one RBI (MLB Stats API result.rbi on that plate appearance). Move-over denominator: plate appearances that begin with a runner on second, nobody on third, and 0 outs. A runner on first is allowed. Base-out state is the first tracked pitch of the plate appearance. Success: the runner who began the plate appearance on second has an end-of-PA state of safe at third (API movement end 3B) or safe at home (end score). He is not successful if he is out, if he never leaves second, or if he only touches third and is then retired. Advancement on the batted ball, a walk, hit-by-pitch, wild pitch, passed ball, balk, or stolen base during the plate appearance all count. A strikeout on which that runner does not end safe at third or home is a failure. QAB is the share of plate appearances with more than 5 pitches (6 or more Statcast pitches). Each month is indexed to that month’s MLB rates. Last-10 rows use full-season 2026 MLB rates, because those games are not one shared month. 2026 MLB RISP knock-in rate was 24.2% (n=43,715 PA). 2026 MLB 0-out, second-to-third move-over rate was 56.2% (n=5,629 PA). 2026 MLB QAB rate (more than 5 pitches) was 20.6% (n=183,849 PA). September 2026 MLB RISP knock-in rate was 25.0% (n=6,463). September move-over rate was 55.8% (n=847). September QAB rate was 21.0% (n=27,294). Also indexed the same way: 2026 barrel% 7.7%, damage rate 22.2%, in-zone whiff 13.9%, chase 30.3%. September barrel% 7.7%, damage rate 22.1%, in-zone whiff 14.2%, chase 30.4%.
color_note: White band is within 10% of the comparison league rate, inclusive (ratio 0.90 to 1.10). For the composite, that is 90 to 110. Small sample: under 8 tracked batted balls for contact quality; under 10 in-zone swings, out-of-zone pitches, or plate-appearance opportunities for the other columns. Execution is a small sample when PA, RISP PA, or move-over PA is under 10. Santurce hitter cards color a continuous blue-to-red magnitude scale (rateHeatStyle in pregame.html). This sheet uses the requested direction instead: white at the league band, green when the rate is better, red when it is worse. Header navy #122C6F matches the Santurce licey navy. Cell green and red are light fills so the numbers stay readable; they are not the Santurce magnitude gradient.
roster_note: MLB Stats API active roster, every day from 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30: 22 position players were active on at least one of those days, and 19 pitchers are excluded. September 30 alone listed 21 position players. Added versus that Sept 30 snapshot: Alex Jackson. Removed versus the earlier 14-name sheet, because they were not on the active roster on any September day: James Outman, Mickey Gasper, Ryan Fitzgerald. Added versus that earlier sheet: Victor Caratini, Kaelen Culpepper, Gabriel Gonzalez, Tristan Gray, Ryan Jeffers, Walker Jenkins, Hendry Mendez, Alan Roden, Emmanuel Rodriguez, Ben Ross, Aaron Sabato. Last-10 games can predate September when that is when the hitter last played. A month with no plate appearances is a blank row.
coverage_note: Schedule finals: 2,429 regular-season games, 2026-03-25 through 2026-09-27. Statcast covered 2,429 of those game pks (100.0%). Plate appearances: 183,849. API join on game and at-bat (Statcast at_bat_number = API atBatIndex + 1, same batter): 100.0%. Batter-id mismatches: 0.
sources_note: Roster, schedule, transactions, RBI, and runner movement: MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com), public endpoints, no login. Pitches, zones, swing descriptions, exit velocity, launch angle, and the barrel flag (launch_speed_angle = 6): Baseball Savant Statcast, downloaded with pybaseball and cached under /Users/colbymorris/TwinsAdvance/cache/statcast. Play-by-play extracts cached under /Users/colbymorris/TwinsAdvance/cache/pbp. Regular season only (schedule gameType=R and Statcast game_type=R).
blank_note: Cells are blank when the denominator is zero or, for the composite, when any of the three input rates is undefined. A month with no plate appearances is a blank row, with no zero rates. Archetype contact cells are blank when the hitter has fewer than 30 competitive batted balls. No rate was imputed from a nearby player, from a career norm, or from memory.
